sections.heading: Market Context & Positioning
sections.text:
Following the recent geopolitical flare-up over the weekend, the Nifty fell roughly 2–3% and left an open gap around the 23,900 level, which the index is now attempting to fill. The advisors indicated that if the situation resolves, a further 5–6% up-move is plausible.
360 ONE remains positive on pharma and infrastructure. Within infra the bias is toward Adani names; within pharma the emphasis is on diagnostics/labs and select formulations. Given expected volatility over the next 10–15 days, the team recommended a portfolio cleanup to create liquidity and deploy it in tranches over the next two to six months.

sections.heading: Sector & Stock-Level Views
sections.text:
Pharma — labs / diagnostics preferred over hospitals
Hospitals viewed as expensive at current levels. Apollo (~₹8,900) considered rich; Max Healthcare flagged as a preferred alternative if a hospital position is taken.
Diagnostics preferred. Thyrocare is the top pick — asset-light, B2B-focused model, low debt versus peers (Metropolis, Dr. Lal PathLabs), and strong rural market share. Vijaya Diagnostic also viewed positively.
Names added / held in portfolio: Sun Pharma and Dr. Reddy's / DRL (~₹20 L each), plus diagnostics. Pharma index showing relative strength even in a weak week.
Infrastructure & MTAR
MTAR Technologies — ₹5 L purchased on the day of the meeting (stock at 5% lower circuit). Positioned as a data-centre / fuel-cell proxy; sole Indian supplier of fuel-cell technology to Bloom Energy.
Concentration risk noted: ~60% of MTAR revenue comes from Bloom Energy; company is diversifying toward other US clients. Order book growing aggressively; next 2–3 years expected to be strong.
Large-caps — Reliance, GEO (Jio Financial), IT
Reliance / GEO (Jio Financial): GEO's numbers do not yet justify near-term alpha; better NBFC opportunities exist (Chola, Bajaj Finance). Reliance not a sell at current price, but trim on any pullback. The future telecom/platform listing is seen as the better way to play the Reliance complex.
HCL Tech / large-cap IT: Limited re-rating triggers given AI-driven disruption in large-cap IT services. Suggestion to book some profit and pivot toward mid-cap IT with better AI adaptability — Persistent Systems and Coforge cited. Traditional IT could de-rate toward pre-COVID multiples (12–13x).
Client takeaway: consider booking partial profit in HCL Tech and reallocating, as it is seen as neither a data-centre/AI nor a clear technology play.
Sugar sector
Balrampur Chini — tracked closely. After the run-up to ~₹600, the team prefers to accumulate on a pullback: nibble around ₹580, complete allocation in the ~₹560–580 range, to stay within risk-management discipline. Catalysts: ethanol demand and PLI. A modest (not disproportionately overweight) allocation is supported.
A second sugar name (transcribed as “Bhagavath Pochini”) was cited as the PM's preferred sector pick on biodegradable-plastics and ethanol triggers. [Name garbled in transcript — verify actual company before acting.]
Triveni noted as having a demerger catalyst; PLI facility for one name expected to commission around Sep–Oct with an order book covering 2–3 years.

sections.heading: REITs, InvITs & Private Credit
sections.text:
Listed REIT/InvIT yields are compressed (not expected above ~7%) due to high demand. New listed REIT purchases paused.
Preferred route to REIT/InvIT is via unlisted / fund structures — but unlisted supply is currently exhausted. A potential third fund (prior two closed at ₹22,000 Cr each) may be brought to the team if launched.
361 RISE fund (private credit) proposed as the alternative: headline IRR ~14%, structured FMT-like with day-one visibility and locked yield. At the 25.17% corporate marginal rate, estimated post-expense / post-tax net return in the ~9–10% range — attractive versus the 6–7% REIT/InvIT yields.
InvIT allocations to be parked until a suitable fund is available.

sections.heading: Unlisted Equity
sections.text: 360 ONE generally avoids unlisted holdings due to liquidity/lock-in risk unless the business is a clear monopoly. Attractive unlisted supply is currently scarce. Names raised in discussion (e.g. via an ICICI contact) were not endorsed; caution advised.

sections.heading: Portfolio Construction — Active vs Passive
sections.text:
Factor / passive funds have underperformed through the recent cycle; momentum and value gains largely reversed. The team favours active managers who can be nimble in choppy markets.
On banking: advised against adding bank-sector funds/ETFs directly given PSU-bank sensitivity in an El Niño year; prefer active management with room to be nimble.
Recommended manager set referenced: Bandhan (Large / Mid Cap), SBI Focused, ICICI, and others noted as outperforming passives in the current phase.

sections.heading: Yield Optimisation — ARISE / RISE Switch
sections.text: The team compared a ~₹2.5 Cr fixed-income line currently yielding ~6.8–7% pre-expense against the RISE/ARISE fund at a stated ~14% IRR. After ~90 paise expense and corporate tax at 25.17%, the estimated net advantage is ~2.8–3% in favour of the move — characterised as a clear switch. The suggested action is to lift the existing SDL-maturity and accrual basket into the RISE fund.

sections.heading: Exit vs Hold — Expiring Bonds
sections.text: On bonds/positions expiring around April 2027: since these are mutual-fund vehicles rather than hold-to-maturity instruments, there is no additional yield alpha in holding them. The team will prepare a deck of recommended ideas and an exit list for review.

sections.heading: Discussion — Portfolio Gap Analysis
sections.text:
5.1  Equity Portfolio Issues
5.1.1  Sectoral Fund Risk — Disproportionate Volatility
MINUTES OF MEETING   ·   360 ONE Asset Management   ·   SMC Family Office Portfolio Review  ·  May 08, 2026
● The portfolio contains a meaningful allocation to sectoral and thematic equity funds. 360 ONE's
analysis reveals that sectoral funds are structurally riskier than diversified funds in two measurable
ways:
◦ Return consistency: Sectoral funds are 3 times more likely to post a negative annual return
compared to well-diversified equity funds — reflecting their dependence on a single sector's cycle.
◦ Volatility: Sectoral funds exhibit 5.5% higher annualised volatility than diversified alternatives — a
meaningful drag on risk-adjusted returns for a portfolio of this size.
● Recommendation: Exit sectoral fund allocations. Replace with diversified high-conviction strategies
(360 ONE PMS or SIFs) that offer better risk-adjusted return profiles without single-sector
dependency.

5.1.2  Active Large-Cap Funds — High Benchmark Overlap
● Several active large-cap mutual funds in the portfolio exhibit excessive overlap with their
benchmark indices — raising fundamental questions about whether active management fees are
justified.
● Example identified: Nippon India Large Cap Fund carries approximately 62% benchmark overlap,
meaning nearly two-thirds of the portfolio mirrors the passive index. At the management fees
charged for active management, this represents poor value for money.
● Recommendation: Replace high-overlap active large-cap funds with lower-cost passive index
alternatives (ETFs or index funds). The savings in management fees compound meaningfully over
time at ₹300 Cr scale.

5.1.3  Fund Proliferation — The Long Tail Problem
● The portfolio currently holds 55+ individual funds. A significant number of these holdings represent
less than 1% of total equity AUM — positions so small that even exceptional performance would
have a negligible impact on overall portfolio returns.
● These sub-threshold positions add disproportionate administrative complexity, increase the number
of capital gains events during rebalancing, and dilute management attention.
● Immediate consolidation plan: Exit all holdings below the 1% AUM threshold. Redirect capital into
existing high-conviction positions or the new three-pillar strategy described in Section 6.

5.2  Debt Portfolio Issues
5.2.1  Target Maturity Funds — Inadequate Yields
● The portfolio holds Target Maturity Funds (TMFs) with maturity dates in 2027. These funds were
appropriate when purchased in a higher-yield environment, but the current effective yield post-
fees of approximately 5.8–6.8% is suboptimal.
● At 5.8–6.8% post-fee yield, these funds are barely keeping pace with inflation (RBI's CPI target: 4–
6%) while occupying significant capital that could generate 8–10% post-tax in Conservative SIFs or
14–16% in Credit AIFs.
● Since these funds are approaching maturity in 2027, the decision on whether to exit early (and
crystallise any mark-to-market impact) vs. hold-to-maturity requires a precise post-tax return
comparison — which 360 ONE will prepare as a prioritised debt fund exit list.

5.2.2  Long-Duration Funds — Interest Rate Sensitivity Risk
● The portfolio holds long-duration debt funds — specifically the Nippon India Nivesh Lakshya Fund —
which are highly sensitive to interest rate movements.
MINUTES OF MEETING   ·   360 ONE Asset Management   ·   SMC Family Office Portfolio Review  ·  May 08, 2026
● In a rising interest rate environment (which remains a live risk given global central bank stances),
these funds experience significant mark-to-market (MTM) paper losses as bond prices fall inversely
with yields. This creates unrealised losses that may crystallise if the position needs to be
liquidated.
● Recommendation: Exit long-duration fund positions as part of the debt overhaul. Proceeds to be
redeployed into shorter-duration instruments or Conservative SIFs which do not carry duration risk.

5.3  Data Discrepancy — Critical Finding
A significant and material data discrepancy was identified during the meeting that undermines the
reliability of all performance comparisons made to date:

Fund 360 ONE IRR SMC Team IRR
ICICI PSU Fund 7.15% 16.67%

● Root cause of the discrepancy: The SMC team's calculation of 16.67% includes returns from past,
already-sold holdings in the ICICI PSU Fund — inflating the apparent current IRR. 360 ONE's figure of
7.15% reflects only the currently held position's return.
● Neither calculation is 'wrong' — but they are measuring different things. Using different baselines
for the same fund creates a fundamentally misleading picture for decision-making.
Resolution Agreed
All future portfolio analysis, fund comparisons, and rebalancing decisions will use a single agreed-
upon data source and calculation methodology. 360 ONE will update their presentation to include
all financial values and explanatory notes. An alignment meeting between the SMC team and 360
ONE's analyst team will be scheduled specifically to establish and document the agreed data
standards.

sections.heading: Discussion — Proposed Portfolio Restructuring
sections.text:
360 ONE proposed a three-pillar restructuring framework to replace the current fragmented 55+ fund
portfolio. Each pillar addresses a specific gap in the current allocation:

6.1  Pillar 1 — Direct Equity PMS (360 ONE)
● The SMC Family Office currently holds approximately ₹4–5 Crore in direct equity positions spread
across individual stocks — a 'long tail' of direct holdings that are difficult to monitor systematically
and lack a coherent investment thesis.
● 360 ONE proposes consolidating this direct equity tail into their Direct Equity PMS — a curated,
actively managed portfolio of high-conviction stock ideas managed by 360 ONE's research team.
● Investment strategy within the PMS focuses on bottom-up stock selection across four high-
conviction secular themes:
◦ Made in India / Manufacturing: Beneficiaries of India's PLI schemes and import substitution drive.
◦ Defence: Domestic defence manufacturing and indigenisation under Atmanirbhar Bharat.
◦ Solar & Clean Energy: India's renewable energy buildout and global decarbonisation transition.
◦ Artificial Intelligence: Indian technology companies and infrastructure beneficiaries of the global
AI cycle.
MINUTES OF MEETING   ·   360 ONE Asset Management   ·   SMC Family Office Portfolio Review  ·  May 08, 2026
● Execution plan: Begin with a ₹1 Crore pilot allocation to stress-test operational efficiency —
specifically the account opening process, trade reporting, and portfolio statement delivery. Upon
satisfactory completion, a larger ₹5 Crore top-up allocation will follow.
● Pre-condition for execution: Sanskar to provide 360 ONE with entity-wise unrealised profit data
from the existing direct equity holdings. This allows 360 ONE to sequence exits in a tax-efficient
manner before transferring capital into the PMS.

6.2  Pillar 2 — Conservative SIFs (Specialised Investment Funds)
Conservative SIFs are presented as the primary replacement vehicle for the portfolio's low-yield debt
mutual funds. The rationale is compelling on both a return and tax efficiency basis:

Metric Current Debt MFs Conservative SIFs
Post-Tax Yield 5.8–6.8% 8–10% (target)
Tax Treatment Marginal rate (~30–39%) Equity LTCG: 12.5%
Strategy Plain vanilla debt Arbitrage + derivatives
Alpha over arbitrage — ~2–3% additional
Duration Risk High (long-duration) Low (hedged)

● Mechanism: SIFs employ arbitrage strategies (simultaneous cash and futures market positions)
combined with derivative overlays to generate consistent alpha of approximately 2–3% above pure
arbitrage fund returns — while maintaining a low-volatility, capital-protection orientation.
● Tax advantage: SIFs use a pass-through taxation structure where gains are treated as equity capital
gains — 12.5% Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) after 1 year vs. the marginal tax rate of
approximately 30–39% applicable to debt mutual fund gains. At the SMC Family Office's tax bracket,
this difference is equivalent to approximately 3–5% additional post-tax return.
● Specific fund cited: Edelweiss Alteva Hybrid Long-Short SIF was highlighted for its track record of
stability and consistent returns. Performance data (1M: +0.79%, 3M: +0.91%, 2026 YTD: +1.09%)
compares favourably against equity savings fund peers which are deeply negative in the same
period.
● Quantum: Capital released from the debt mutual fund exit programme will be the primary source
of funding for SIF allocations.

6.3  Pillar 3 — Unlisted REITs (Alt-R PMS)
● To address the portfolio's near-zero allocation to real assets, 360 ONE presented an unlisted REIT
opportunity via the Alt-R PMS platform as the third strategic pillar.
6.3.1  Investment Thesis
● The unlisted REIT invests in Grade-A commercial properties (office, logistics, data centres) at pre-
listing valuations. The return architecture has two components:
◦ Current income: Rental yield from tenanted Grade-A assets, providing regular cash flow during the
investment period.
◦ Capital appreciation: Significant valuation re-rating expected upon eventual REIT listing on the
stock exchange — where comparable listed REITs trade at meaningful premiums to NAV.
● Target return: 15–21% pre-tax IRR over the investment horizon — substantially above listed REIT
returns (typically 8–12% p.a.) due to the pre-listing entry valuation advantage.
6.3.2  Client Due Diligence Concerns
MINUTES OF MEETING   ·   360 ONE Asset Management   ·   SMC Family Office Portfolio Review  ·  May 08, 2026
● Mr. Sunil Goel raised three specific due diligence questions that require 360 ONE's formal written
response before any commitment:
◦ Fire insurance: Is adequate fire and property damage insurance maintained on all underlying
assets? What are the coverage limits and which insurer?
◦ Loss of rent coverage: Does the insurance structure include loss of rent provisions that protect
cash yield continuity in the event of a property incident?
◦ Vacancy allowance: How does the fund model vacancy risk? What is the assumed vacancy rate, and
how are gaps in rental income managed during tenant transitions?
● These are standard commercial real estate due diligence items. 360 ONE to confirm all three in
writing before the SMC team makes any allocation decision.
6.3.3  Time Sensitivity
Subscription Deadline: May 15, 2026
The current fundraising window for the Alt-R PMS unlisted REIT fund closes on May 15, 2026 — seven
days from the date of this meeting. The due diligence responses from 360 ONE must be received
and reviewed by the SMC team by May 12–13, 2026 at the latest to allow time for an informed
decision before the deadline.

sections.heading: Discussion — Macro Rationale & Global Allocation
sections.text:
The proposed portfolio restructuring is grounded in a clear macro framework articulated by the 360 ONE
team:

U N D E R W E I G H T
United States
▸ Record high fiscal deficit and sovereign debt
▸ Persistent inflation risk from tariff policy
▸ Equity valuations at historical extremes
O V E R W E I G H T
China · Europe · India
▸ China: deep value, stimulus-driven recovery
▸ Europe: post-Ukraine reconstruction cycle
▸ India: secular growth, earnings visibility

● This macro framework directly informs the equity PMS strategy (India-focused, Made in India
themes) and validates the existing international equity allocation increase already underway
following earlier advisor meetings.
● No specific action items arise from the macro discussion — it serves as the conviction framework
underlying all three investment pillars proposed by 360 ONE.

sections.heading: Discussion — Structured Review Process

sections.heading: Discussion — Portfolio Analysis & Key Findings
sections.text:
4.1  Current Asset Allocation Snapshot
The portfolio was reviewed at an aggregate level. The broad asset allocation at the time of the
meeting is summarised below:

Asset Class Approximate Allocation
Equity (Domestic + International) ~57%
Fixed Income (Debt MFs, AIFs, Bonds) ~27%
Cash & Alternates (REITs, Commodities, etc.) ~16%

4.2  Identified Portfolio Issues
4.2.1  Over-Diversification & Long-Tail Problem
● The portfolio contains in excess of 100 individual holdings across mutual funds, PMS
strategies, AIFs, REITs, INVITs, and commodities.
● A significant "long tail" of positions each representing less than 1% of total portfolio value
exists. These holdings generate negligible portfolio-level impact but add substantial
administrative and monitoring burden.
MINUTES OF MEETING   |   Shriram Wealth Advisory   |   Family Office Portfolio Review
● Decision taken: All holdings below the agreed minimum threshold will be exited systematically.
Tax-loss harvesting opportunities will be assessed simultaneously to offset capital gains
elsewhere in the portfolio.

4.2.2  AMC Concentration Risk
● Approximately 30% of the mutual fund AUM is concentrated with a single AMC — ICICI
Prudential.
● This creates key-man and institutional risk. Specifically noted: the recent departure of senior
fund manager Anish Tawakle from ICICI Prudential, which warrants a review of all ICICI
Prudential fund holdings for continuity of investment philosophy.

4.2.3  Significant Strategy Overlap
● Analysis revealed greater than 50% portfolio overlap between IPRO Balanced Advantage
Fund (BAF) and Edelweiss BAF.
● Holding multiple funds within the same sub-category with near-identical underlying portfolios
provides false diversification and dilutes the intended asset allocation.
● Decision: The inferior-ranked fund (Edelweiss BAF and Kotak BAF) will be exited, retaining
only the higher-conviction BAF choice.

4.2.4  Underperforming Holdings
● DSP Equity Savings Fund is generating a trailing XIRR of approximately 2%, significantly
below the category average and not commensurate with the risk assumed.
● Parag Parikh Flexi Cap was noted as a fund that has not adequately captured market upside in
recent periods relative to its peers.
● Both funds are under review for exit, with capital to be redeployed as per the revised IPS
framework.

4.2.5  Suboptimal Domestic Debt Strategy
● Post-tax yields on domestic debt mutual funds are estimated in the range of 6.5–7.5%,
reflecting significant tax drag.
● This level of return does not adequately compensate investors when compared to available
alternatives such as Credit AIFs and international fixed income vehicles.
● A sensitivity analysis covering YTM, duration, and post-tax comparisons across debt MFs,
hybrids, and AIFs has been requested from Shriram Wealth.

sections.heading: Discussion — Asset Allocation & Strategic Shifts
sections.text:
5.1  International Equity Exposure
● Current international equity allocation stands at approximately 5% of the total portfolio —
significantly below the target.
MINUTES OF MEETING   |   Shriram Wealth Advisory   |   Family Office Portfolio Review
● The team agreed to increase this allocation to a range of 10–15% to achieve genuine
geographic diversification, reduce home-country bias, and participate in global themes such as
artificial intelligence, semiconductors, and other secular growth sectors.
● Appropriate vehicles (existing international MFs, global fund-of-funds, and feeder structures)
will be evaluated in the revised IPS.

5.2  REITs & INVITs
● It was agreed to increase exposure to Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) and
Infrastructure Investment Trusts (INVITs).
● Rationale: These instruments offer partially tax-efficient regular income distributions, act as a
partial hedge to pure equity, and benefit from long-duration infrastructure and real estate
cycles.
● Specific allocation targets and recommended instruments will be included in the revised deck.

5.3  Debt Reallocation Strategy
● The team discussed a structured shift away from low-yield domestic debt mutual funds toward
higher-returning alternatives:
◦ Credit AIFs: Target gross YTM of 14–16%, with appropriate risk/credit assessment. A post-tax
hybrid vs. AIF comparison will be shared by Shriram Wealth.
◦ International Bond Funds: Target YTM of approximately 9–9.25% (with leverage),
denominated in USD with a currency hedge to manage forex risk.
● The proceeds from debt mutual fund exits will be staged to minimise tax impact, leveraging the
grandfathering provisions and holding period benefits where applicable.

5.4  Commodity Rebalancing — Silver to Gold
● Silver positions were acquired historically at approximately ₹50,000 per kg. Current market
price is approximately $75 per troy ounce, representing a meaningful appreciation.
● The narrowing silver supply-demand gap and recent price rally suggest the risk-reward for
holding further upside has diminished.
● Decision: Profits in silver will be booked and proceeds redeployed into gold, which is
considered a more defensible long-duration store of value within the commodities allocation.
● Specific entry levels for gold and exit triggers for silver will be communicated by Dhaval
Kapadia (Shriram Wealth) to Sunil and Sanskar prior to execution.

sections.heading: Discussion — Fund & PMS Review
sections.text:
6.1  Hybrid Fund Rationalisation
● The hybrid mutual fund bucket contains multiple Balanced Advantage Funds (BAFs) with
substantial strategy overlap.
● The agreed approach is to retain a maximum of 2–3 BAFs, selecting only the highest-ranked
based on Shriram Wealth's quantitative framework.
MINUTES OF MEETING   |   Shriram Wealth Advisory   |   Family Office Portfolio Review
● Edelweiss BAF and Kotak BAF are earmarked for exit in the immediate consolidation phase.

6.2  PMS Review — Carnelian Capital
● The portfolio holds an investment of approximately ₹1.5 Crore in the Carnelian Capital "SHIFT"
strategy.
● Carnelian is undergoing a thematic change to the SHIFT strategy, creating uncertainty around
future positioning and mandate continuity.
● The Carnelian "Compounder" strategy was identified as a potentially better fit given its focus
on quality businesses with consistent earnings growth.
● Action: Sunil Goel to directly email Vikas Khemani (Carnelian Capital) to seek clarity on the
SHIFT strategy's revised mandate versus the Compounder strategy. Outcome to be shared
with Sumit and Dhaval at Shriram Wealth.

6.3  HDFC FlexiCap — Manager Transition Monitoring
● HDFC FlexiCap recently underwent a fund manager change, with Roshi Jain being replaced
by Amit Ganatra.
● Fund manager transitions introduce the risk of style drift and portfolio repositioning during the
changeover period.
● The position will be monitored closely over the next 2–3 quarters for any meaningful
divergence from the fund's historical investment philosophy before a hold/exit decision is
made.

6.4  PMS Rationalisation — IPRO Large Cap vs. Contra
● There is noted overlap between the IPRO Large Cap PMS and the Contra PMS strategies.
Holding both dilutes differentiation.
● The team will assess retaining only one, or transitioning to a broader "Opportunities" PMS
mandate that subsumes both exposures.

6.5  Fund Selection Methodology — Shriram Wealth Framework
Shriram Wealth's proprietary fund selection process follows a rigorous two-stage approach:

● Stage 1 — Quantitative Ranking: Shriram Wealth employs a quantitative screening model
applied to all funds with AUM in excess of ₹100 Crore. Funds are ranked using a composite
scorecard covering: 1-year, 3-year, and 5-year rolling returns on a monthly basis; upside and
downside capture ratios relative to the benchmark; and risk-adjusted performance ratios
(Sharpe and Sortino). This quantitative screen produces a ranked shortlist of funds within each
category.
● Stage 2 — Qualitative Analysis: The top-ranked funds from Stage 1 undergo a qualitative
deep-dive. This focuses on fund manager track record and tenure, consistency of investment
philosophy across market cycles, and performance attribution analysis (alpha decomposition).
The alpha attribution exercise is particularly important — it identifies whether a fund's
outperformance is driven by systematic stock selection skill or by sector-level tactical bets.
MINUTES OF MEETING   |   Shriram Wealth Advisory   |   Family Office Portfolio Review
Example cited: Bandhan Small Cap Fund's alpha has been found to originate predominantly
from bottom-up stock selection, indicating a more durable and replicable edge.

sections.heading: Discussion — Investment Policy Statement (IPS) Framework
sections.text:
The IPS was identified as the single most important governance document for the family office going
forward. The current IPS documents (from ICICI, 361 One, and 2OMC) will serve as inputs for a
comprehensive refresh. The revised IPS will embody the following principles:

● Dynamic & Living Document: The revised IPS will move from a static target to a dynamic,
living document subject to formal semi-annual reviews. It will cover all asset classes in scope
and provide a clear decision framework for additions, exits, and rebalancing.
● Core vs. Satellite Architecture: The IPS will delineate between core holdings (long-term,
benchmark-driven, high-conviction) and satellite positions (tactical, thematic, or opportunistic).
Allocation ranges — minimum and maximum — will be defined for each sub-category to
prevent drift.
● Fund Count & Size Guardrails: Clear rules will be embedded regarding the maximum
number of funds permitted per category (e.g., no more than 2–3 BAFs) and a minimum holding
size (in absolute INR terms) below which no new positions will be initiated and existing
positions will be exited.
● Asset Class Target Ranges: Each asset class will carry a defined target range (e.g.,
International Equity: 10–15%, REITs/INVITs: 5–8%, Gold: 3–5%) with a rebalancing trigger
built into the IPS when allocations breach the upper or lower band.

sections.heading: Discussion — Barclays Equity Strategy & Macro View
sections.text:
4.1  Market Volatility & Near-Term Tactical Recovery
● Recent market volatility has resulted in a meaningful repricing of risk across asset classes.
Barclays' view is that as news flow stabilises — particularly around US Fed policy direction,
geopolitical developments, and domestic earnings — a tactical recovery in equities is likely in
the near term.
● However, the team cautioned that this tactical recovery should not be mistaken for a structural
re-rating. Fundamental concerns around global liquidity conditions and earnings growth
sustainability remain.

4.2  FY27 Earnings Outlook — Below Consensus
● Barclays has set their FY27 Nifty earnings growth estimate at approximately 10%, which is
materially below the street consensus range of 13–14%.
● Rationale: The combination of elevated crude oil prices (adding cost pressure across sectors),
sticky global interest rates (compressing credit-funded consumption and capex), and the
lagged impact of FII outflows on corporate confidence justifies a more conservative earnings
trajectory.
● Implication for the SMC portfolio: Avoid chasing broad market indices at current multiples.
Focus capital deployment on specific sectors and stocks where earnings visibility is high and
valuations remain reasonable post-correction.

4.3  Interest Rates & Oil — Key Macro Risks
● The US Federal Reserve is expected to maintain a higher-for-longer interest rate stance —
Barclays does not forecast meaningful rate cuts in the near term. This continues to create a
challenging environment for global risk assets and emerging market flows.
● Brent crude oil risk is assessed in the range of USD 80–85 per barrel. For India — a net oil
importer — sustained crude at these levels adds to the current account deficit, puts upward
pressure on retail inflation, and constrains the RBI's ability to cut rates domestically.

4.4  Preferred Equity Sectors
● Barclays identified four preferred equity pockets for the current environment, categorised by
their conviction level:
◦ Core: BFSI — specifically Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs): Favoured as a core
holding due to improving asset quality, strong loan growth in retail/SME segments, and
attractive valuations relative to PSU banks. NBFCs are seen as primary beneficiaries of a
potential rate-easing cycle when it eventually materialises.
◦ Core: High-End Consumer Discretionary: Premium consumer brands and lifestyle companies
with pricing power and aspirational demand from India's growing affluent and upper-middle-
class segments. Less vulnerable to commodity cost pressures than mass-market consumer
goods.
◦ Tactical: Defence-Adjacent: Companies in the Indian defence supply chain, aerospace, and
indigenisation beneficiaries. Tactical rather than core given valuation re-rating already partially
complete, but structural tailwinds from defence capex remain intact.

◦ Tactical: Metals: Selected metals and mining names benefit from the global commodity
supercycle and China demand recovery. Tactical position given cyclical nature and sensitivity
to global trade and tariff dynamics.

including Defence and Metals. Key team members involved in stock selection include Barclays

The recommended positioning is a tilt toward small-cap with a measured addition of mid-cap.

sections.heading: Discussion — REITs, INVITs & Alternatives
sections.text:
6.1  Strategic Rationale for Increasing Uncorrelated Allocations
● Barclays strongly recommended building the portfolio's allocation to uncorrelated asset classes
— specifically REITs, INVITs, and international equity — toward a combined target of 20–25%
of total portfolio value.
● The SMC portfolio's current exposure to these asset classes is estimated at less than 5%
combined, representing a significant structural gap relative to best-practice multi-asset
construction for a family office of this scale.
● REITs and INVITs provide a combination of regular income distributions (tax-efficient under
current regulations), inflation protection through rent/toll escalation clauses, and low correlation
to domestic equity markets — making them effective portfolio diversifiers.

6.2  Preferred INVIT & REIT Segments
● Barclays ranked infrastructure segments for INVIT/REIT investment by preference:
◦ 1st Priority: Roads / Toll INVITs — Top pick: Stable, contracted cash flows from toll
concessions; embedded inflation protection via annual toll rate escalation; strong capital
appreciation potential as concession values re-rate. Mindspace REIT was specifically
mentioned for the roads/commercial real estate segment.

◦ 2nd Priority: Telecom Towers — Stable rental income from long-term operator lease
agreements; beneficiary of 5G rollout and increasing tower utilisation rates.
◦ 3rd Priority: Warehousing — Strong structural demand from e-commerce, 3PL logistics, and
manufacturing. NDR (National Distribution and Warehousing) highlighted as a specific
opportunity (see Section 6.3).
◦ 4th Priority: Power Transmission / Utilities — Regulated return assets with government-
backed cash flows; lower growth but very high income certainty.

6.3  NDR Warehousing INVIT — Preferential Allotment Opportunity
● NDR (a leading warehousing and logistics infrastructure platform) is conducting a preferential
allotment round for their INVIT structure. This represents a time-sensitive, institutional-access
opportunity with the following indicative terms:
◦ Minimum commitment: approximately ₹5 Crore.
◦ Expected 3-year Internal Rate of Return (IRR): approximately 15%.
◦ Cash yield component: approximately 6–7% per annum (distributed regularly).
◦ Balance of return: capital appreciation as the INVIT NAV re-rates over the 3-year period.
● Tax treatment: REIT and INVIT distributions have a mixed tax structure. Certain distribution
components (interest income from the SPV) are taxed at slab rates, while capital gains from
unit sales are treated under equity-like LTCG rules (12.5% after 1-year holding period). Mutual
fund-classified REITs may have different treatment — detailed tax analysis to be reviewed
before commitment.
● Action: Sanjay (Barclays Alternatives) to circulate the formal NDR preferential allotment term
sheet including detailed minimums, timelines, IRR waterfall, and expected yield profile.

6.4  Multi-Asset Fund Suggestions — Nippon India Japan Fund & Kotak Global
Emerging Markets Omni
● For international equity exposure within the REIT/INVIT/international allocation framework, two
specific fund suggestions were noted from the handwritten discussion:
◦ Nippon India Japan Fund: Provides targeted exposure to the Japanese equity market — one
of the few developed markets with significant potential for valuation re-rating driven by
corporate governance reforms and return of shareholder-friendly practices. Exposure of
approximately 5 lakh per PAN suggested.
◦ Kotak Global Emerging Markets Omni: Diversified emerging market fund providing exposure
across India, China, Brazil, and other EM countries. Suitable for the international equity sleeve
of the portfolio.

● Two specific credit instruments were presented during the meeting:
◦ Wisdom Finance Paper: A short-dated credit instrument at an attractive yield (specific yield

8.1  GIFT City Overview
● Shailendra Sharma introduced GIFT City (Gujarat International Finance Tec-City) as a vehicle
for the SMC family office to access offshore-equivalent investment structures within an Indian
regulatory framework.
● GIFT City offers a unique tax regime: businesses and funds operating within the IFSC
(International Financial Services Centre) in GIFT City enjoy significant tax concessions,
including exemptions on certain capital gains, dividends, and interest income — making it an
attractive domicile for structuring family office investments.
● Two specific GIFT City structures were referenced (from handwritten notes, page 7):
◦ New Bond Structures by Barclays: Barclays and Nippon are developing new bond instruments
accessible through GIFT City, which will offer 20–25 basis points more yield compared to
equivalent domestic structures, while maintaining 15% tax-beneficial treatment for investors.
◦ OPI/ODI Structures: Overseas Portfolio Investment (OPI) and Overseas Direct Investment
(ODI) structures accessible through GIFT City, enabling the SMC family office to deploy
capital into offshore assets with Indian regulatory clarity.

sections.heading: Discussion — FY27 Market Outlook & Geopolitical Risks
sections.text:
5.1  Global Macro Environment — Stagflation Risk
● The dominant macro theme for FY27 is elevated stagflation risk: a combination of persistently
high oil prices and sticky global interest rates that simultaneously suppress growth and keep
inflation elevated.
MINUTES OF MEETING   |   ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund   |   Portfolio Review — SMC Family Office
● India's crude oil import basket reached a lifetime high of $126 per barrel during the period
under review, significantly increasing the country's import bill and current account deficit
pressure. This directly impacts the rupee and corporate margins across energy-intensive
sectors.
● Global central banks — particularly the US Federal Reserve — continue to maintain a high-for-
longer interest rate stance, which restricts global liquidity and makes risk assets relatively less
attractive versus cash and short-duration instruments.

5.2  US Equity — Overvaluation Signals
● The US equity market was assessed as significantly overvalued relative to fundamentals and
global peers. Key evidence cited: Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway has accumulated a
record $380 billion in cash, an implicit signal of limited attractive investment opportunities at
current US market prices.
● Other markets flagged as carrying elevated risk include South Korea (concentrated
AI/semiconductor exposure) and Taiwan (TSMC-specific systemic risk and ongoing
geopolitical tensions).
● Decision: US equity allocation within the portfolio will be reduced, with proceeds redeployed to
more attractively valued markets.

5.3  Foreign Institutional Investor (FII) Activity
● FIIs sold a record ₹95,000 Crore worth of Indian equities in March 2026, representing one of
the largest monthly outflows in recent history. Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs) and retail
flows through SIPs have absorbed this selling pressure thus far.
● However, the sustainability of DII absorption is uncertain. If domestic retail flows slow — for
example, due to a sentiment shift driven by further market weakness — the absence of FII
support could accelerate the correction.
● The team noted that India's trailing price-to-earnings multiple of approximately 24x in late 2024
was significantly elevated relative to other emerging markets trading at 7–11x, which
contributed to the FII reallocation away from India. Valuations have since compressed but
remain relatively elevated.

5.4  Rupee Outlook
● The Indian Rupee is expected to trade in a range of 91–96 against the US Dollar over the near
to medium term.
● The RBI is not expected to undertake significant rate cuts in the immediate term, given the
inflationary pressures from high crude oil prices. This limits the scope for a material re-rating of
rate-sensitive domestic sectors.
● For international investments denominated in USD (such as the Silverdale fund and global
equity allocations), the expected rupee range reinforces the attractiveness of maintaining and
growing the offshore allocation as a natural currency hedge.

sections.text:

6.1  Equity — Increase from 58% to 60–63%
● Rationale: The market correction of the past several months has created selective buying
opportunities, particularly in mid-cap and small-cap segments where drawdowns of 15–18%
and 20–25% respectively have brought valuations to more reasonable levels.
● Quantum: The incremental equity deployment will represent approximately 5% of the total
portfolio, estimated at approximately ₹15 Crore in absolute terms.
● Fund selection methodology: Rather than adding to new funds, the team will prioritise topping
up existing holdings in funds that have experienced the deepest drawdowns since February
28, 2026. This averaging-down approach reduces the average cost of acquisition in positions
already held with conviction. Adesh will prepare a fund-by-fund drawdown analysis and identify
5 priority funds for the incremental deployment.
● All fund additions require prior analysis of the underlying portfolio to avoid inadvertently adding
to funds with significant exposure to sectors or themes the team is cautious on (e.g.,
overvalued large-caps, US-facing IT exporters).

6.2  IT Sector — Increase Allocation to Index Weight
● The portfolio's current IT sector allocation stands at approximately 6.5%, meaningfully below
the IT sector's weight in the Nifty index of approximately 9.5%.
● Rationale for increasing IT allocation: The sector is considered a re-rating candidate. IT
companies are currently trading at cash flow yields of 5–6%, which is attractive on an absolute
basis. Additionally, recent changes to tax rules around on-exchange share buybacks make this
mechanism more tax-efficient for companies, increasing the likelihood of capital returns to
shareholders and providing price support.
● Action: IT allocation to be increased to approximately 9.5% (Nifty index weight) through
targeted additions to existing IT-focused funds or direct stock positions.

6.3  International Equity — Reduce US, Rotate to India IT / China
● US equity exposure will be reduced as part of the broader risk reduction and valuation
discipline exercise.
● Proceeds will be redeployed across two identified opportunities:
◦ Indian IT: Benefits from a weaker rupee (export earnings are dollar-denominated), reasonable
valuations after the recent correction, and structural growth in technology outsourcing. The
sector also benefits from the buyback tax change mentioned above.
◦ China: Despite elevated geopolitical risk, Chinese equities are trading at deeply discounted
multiples (7–10x earnings) relative to historical levels and global peers. The risk-reward is
considered favourable on a selective basis, particularly in consumer and technology sectors
that have undergone significant regulatory normalisation.
● Action: Adesh to execute the US equity sale and initiate reallocation to India IT / China
exposure.

6.4  Bullion Rebalancing — Silver to Gold
● Current bullion allocation: Silver at 5% of portfolio, Gold at 2% of portfolio.
● Target allocation post-rebalancing: Silver reduced to 4%, Gold increased to 3%.
MINUTES OF MEETING   |   ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund   |   Portfolio Review — SMC Family Office
● Rationale: Gold is a superior defensive hedge in a stagflation or global recession scenario due
to its lower industrial demand component and stronger safe-haven credentials. Silver's recent
extraordinary rally (+151% XIRR in FY26) has already captured significant upside, and the
narrowing supply-demand gap suggests returns from current levels will be more modest.
● Execution plan: Sell approximately ₹5 Crore of silver in tranches of ₹25 Lakh per day over 15
trading days to minimise market impact and achieve a favourable average exit price. Gold
purchases to be executed simultaneously.
● Action: Adesh to coordinate and execute the silver-to-gold switch over the next 2–3 weeks.

6.5  New Opportunity — US Agricultural Commodity ETFs
● The team discussed a new thematic investment opportunity in US agricultural commodity ETFs
— specifically exposure to corn, soybean, wheat, and sugar via Wisdom Tree ETF products.
● Rationale: Agricultural commodities are considered one of the few mispriced asset classes
globally at current prices. A key structural driver is the use of corn and sugarcane as
feedstocks for ethanol and biodiesel — making agri commodities indirect beneficiaries of the
sustained high oil price environment. As energy prices remain elevated, the economics of

sections.heading: Discussion — Client Objectives & Portfolio Review
sections.text:
4.1  Investment Philosophy & Primary Goal
Mr. Goel articulated a clear and ambitious investment philosophy: the family office portfolio should
function as an active "profit centre" for long-term wealth creation — not merely as a capital
preservation vehicle. He expressed a preference for decisive, conviction-driven portfolio construction
over the current approach of broad diversification across a large number of smaller positions. The
target equity allocation of 60–65% reflects this growth orientation, with the balance deployed across
global fixed income, alternatives, and commodities.

4.2  Monthly Cash Flow & Deployment
● The family office generates approximately ₹2 Crore in monthly cash flow, which will serve as
the primary engine for systematic deployment into the revised portfolio structure.
● Cash flow will be allocated to priority areas identified in the revised IPS, including international
equity funds, Credit AIFs, and global fixed income instruments.
● A same-day reinvestment discipline will be enforced to ensure proceeds from exits are
immediately redeployed, preventing drag on portfolio returns.

4.3  Key Issues Identified in the Current Portfolio
4.3.1  Over-Diversification
● The portfolio currently holds in excess of 100 individual positions. This level of fragmentation is
counterproductive — it dilutes the impact of high-conviction positions, increases monitoring
complexity, and creates a long tail of holdings that are too small to influence overall returns.
● Agreed resolution: The portfolio will be condensed to no more than 15 funds across all asset
classes, with each fund carrying a meaningful minimum allocation in absolute rupee terms.

4.3.2  Performance Overlap & False Diversification
● Analysis revealed a 44–50% portfolio overlap between hybrid funds from the same AMC (ICICI
Prudential). Holding multiple funds with near-identical underlying portfolios within the same
AMC creates a false sense of diversification without genuine risk reduction.
● This structural redundancy will be eliminated in the consolidation phase by retaining only the
highest-ranked fund in each sub-category.

4.3.3  Key-Man & AMC Concentration Risk
● The portfolio carries significant concentration risk due to overexposure to ICICI Prudential
across both mutual funds and PMS strategies.
● The recent departure of Anish Tawakli, a key senior fund manager at ICICI Prudential, has
heightened concerns around continuity of investment philosophy in the affected funds.
● Diversification across AMCs and fund managers is a priority in the revised portfolio structure.

4.3.4  Debt Fund Taxation Trap
● A material portion of the portfolio is held in debt mutual funds acquired prior to the April 2023
tax amendment, which removed the indexation benefit from debt fund gains.
● Exiting these funds now would crystallise tax liability without the previously available indexation
offset, making a direct switch financially suboptimal in many cases.
● Shriram Wealth has been asked to model the post-tax return of holding these funds to maturity
versus switching to alternative instruments, so that an informed, tax-efficient decision can be
made.

targeting a maximum of 15 funds across the entire portfolio.
● The proposal will include a tax impact analysis for each proposed exit, covering short-term
capital gains (STCG), long-term capital gains (LTCG), and applicable surcharges.
● Exits from underperforming or sub-threshold holdings will be sequenced to offset gains with
available losses (tax-loss harvesting), and reinvestment will be executed on the same day to
maintain market exposure.

● To address key-man and AMC concentration risk, the team recommends introducing an
alternative PMS strategy alongside or in replacement of certain ICICI Prudential PMS
positions.
● The Opportunities (OEO) PMS was specifically highlighted as a candidate — it carries a 10-

same key-man dependency risk as the ICICI Prudential strategies.
● A detailed PMS peer comparison (including returns, risk metrics, and manager track record)

5.3  Non-Discretionary PMS (NDPMS)
● Shriram Wealth introduced the concept of a Non-Discretionary PMS (NDPMS) as an efficient
mechanism for managing the client's direct mutual fund plans.
● Under this structure, the PMS manager proposes all trades (entries, exits, and switches) but
executes them only after obtaining explicit client consent for each transaction.
● Key benefits: (a) access to lower-cost direct mutual fund plans rather than regular plans, (b)
professional portfolio management and rebalancing discipline, (c) consolidated reporting
across all holdings, and (d) full client control and transparency.
● The fee structure for the NDPMS will be shared separately by Dhaval Kapadia.

5.4.1  Fund Overview
● Silverdale Capital Pte Ltd (Singapore, MAS-regulated) manages the Silverdale Target Return
Fund June 2029, a fixed-tenure, USD-denominated bond fund structured as a Variable Capital
Company (VCC) under Singapore law. The fund is available to accredited and institutional
investors only.
● Launch date: January 30, 2026. Maturity: June 2029 (approximately 3.5-year tenure). This
fixed-tenure structure provides investors with visibility on the investment horizon and exit date.
5.4.2  Investment Strategy & Portfolio
● The fund invests in a diversified portfolio of 30–60 US dollar-denominated bonds across 12+
countries, with a primary focus on investment-grade credit (BBB 48%, A 4%) and selective
exposure to BB-rated bonds (approximately 41%) to enhance yield.

assessment of the current asset allocation against the client's Balanced risk profile, including
identification of structural inefficiencies and concentration risks; (2) a review of existing PMS and
fund performance across all mandates; and (3) a set of specific, actionable portfolio
recommendations spanning equity, fixed income, alternatives, and bullion. The meeting was data-
driven — featuring quantitative performance comparisons, post-tax yield analysis, and SIF
(Specialised Investment Fund) performance data — enabling concrete, prioritised decision-making
for the near term.

SG Family Office 3.3 Nifty 500 Equal Weight Index Fund — Misclassified Risk
The Nifty 500 Equal Weight Index Fund has been included in the portfolio, potentially under the assumption that it provides large-cap stability. This is a misconception that requires correction.

The Nifty 500 Equal Weight fund assigns uniform weight to all 500 constituents — meaning approximately 75% of the portfolio is effectively tilted toward mid-cap and small-cap stocks (which constitute the majority of the Nifty 500 by count). This is fundamentally different from the cap-weighted Nifty 50 or Nifty 100, which are dominated by large-cap holdings.

Additionally, the equal-weight methodology requires periodic rebalancing back to uniform weights, which generates higher tracking error and transaction costs compared to a standard cap-weighted index fund. Since then, the IRR on these duration funds has compressed to the range of 5–7% — now essentially matching the return available from arbitrage funds, which carry significantly lower risk (market-neutral strategy with minimal duration exposure).

● Short-Term High-Yield Bonds are recommended to replace pure arbitrage fund exposure,
capturing the 220 basis point post-tax yield advantage (7.32% vs 5.10%) with modestly higher

4.3  Reduce ICICI Active & Passive Asset Allocator FoF
● The ICICI Active & Passive Asset Allocator Fund of Funds is a unique structure that allocates
exclusively to other ICICI Prudential funds — both active and passive variants. While marketed
as a diversified multi-strategy solution, it functionally deepens AMC concentration by directing
capital entirely within the ICICI ecosystem.
● The compounding effect of this FoF on AMC concentration is non-linear: every rupee in the
FoF generates further ICICI Pru AUM within the same portfolio. This is diametrically opposed
to the portfolio's requirement to reduce ICICI Pru dependency.
● Recommendation: Reduce or fully exit the ICICI Active & Passive Asset Allocator FoF.
Redeploy proceeds into direct exposure to a diversified set of funds from non-ICICI AMCs, or
into the recommended SIFs and healthcare PMS.

4.4  Exit IT/ITes Sectoral — Rotate to Healthcare & BFSI
● The IT/ITes sectoral fund allocation should be exited based on three converging headwinds:
◦ AI Disruption: Generative AI and automation are beginning to structurally reduce demand for
traditional software services outsourcing — the core revenue driver for Indian IT majors. This
is not a cyclical slowdown but a potential structural shift in the IT services market.
◦ Delayed Enterprise Spending: Global enterprise technology budgets remain constrained as
CFOs prioritise cost optimisation over new IT projects in a high-interest-rate, uncertain macro
environment.
◦ Valuation Compression: IT sector P/E multiples and forward earnings estimates have been
revised downward, limiting near-term price upside even if the macro environment improves.
● Rotation target — two sectors with strong structural tailwinds:
◦ Indian Healthcare: Domestic formulation demand, hospital sector expansion, MedTech
growth, and global API supply chain diversification (away from China) are driving a multi-year
structural growth story. Valuation re-rating is still in early stages. InCred Healthcare PMS is
the recommended vehicle.
◦ BFSI (particularly NBFCs): Credit penetration remains low relative to GDP; NBFC balance
sheets have strengthened post-2019 crisis; the eventual rate-easing cycle will benefit NBFCs
disproportionately. Already a core holding in the portfolio — recommend increasing allocation.

4.5  Trim Bullion — Silver 50–75%, Review Gold
● The bullion allocation has been an outstanding performer and is now due for strategic profit
booking:
◦ Silver: Has delivered an extraordinary 49% IRR since 2023 versus the BSE 500's
approximately 13% over the same period. The risk-reward for holding silver at current price
levels has significantly deteriorated — the easy money has been made, and mean-reversion
risk is elevated. Recommendation: Trim silver by 50–75% of current allocation and redeploy
proceeds into equities at corrected levels.
◦ Gold: Has also delivered a strong 36% IRR — well above long-run averages. While gold's
defensive properties remain intact (and are actually valuable in the current macro
environment), the magnitude of recent returns suggests some profit-booking is appropriate.
The team flagged this as a review item rather than a firm exit recommendation.
● Redeployment of bullion proceeds: Capital released from silver trimming should be
systematically reinvested into equities — specifically into the funds and themes that have
experienced the deepest corrections (mid/small cap mutual funds, healthcare sector) and into
the SIF products recommended above.

4.6  Diversify Equity Alternates — Unlisted & Private Equity
● The Equity Alternates bucket (currently 5% of AUM, entirely in NSE unlisted shares) is under-
diversified. Concentration in a single unlisted asset creates binary risk — the portfolio either
benefits significantly from an NSE IPO or faces illiquidity and valuation uncertainty in the
interim.
● Recommendation: Introduce curated unlisted equity and private equity exposure via
professionally managed solutions. This could include:
◦ Pre-IPO funds with diversified portfolios across multiple unlisted companies.
◦ Private equity funds with access to growth-stage Indian businesses.
◦ Venture capital or late-stage venture funds for technology and healthcare sector exposure at
early valuation entry points.
MINUTES OF MEETING   |   InCred Wealth   |   Investment Review — M/s. SG Family Office
● Professional management is critical in this asset class — self-managed unlisted portfolios
carry significant information asymmetry and valuation risk. A fund-based approach provides
diversification, independent governance, and regular reporting.

4.7  Add to FI Alternates — Special Situations & Venture Credit
● The FI Alternates bucket (15% of AUM) currently consists of approximately 6% high-yield
credit (NCDs and AIFs) and approximately 2% REIT/CRE. This allocation can be enhanced
through two additional credit themes:
◦ Special Situations Credit: Structured credit investments in companies undergoing business
transitions, asset monetisation, or distressed-but-recoverable scenarios. These typically offer
14–18% IRR with well-secured collateral structures and defined exit mechanisms.
◦ Venture Credit / Venture Debt: Debt instruments issued to late-stage startups and venture-
backed companies, secured against future equity raises or underlying assets. Typically
structured with interest rates of 15–20% plus equity warrants, providing a yield-plus-upside
return profile that is uncorrelated to public markets.
● Both themes are consistent with the portfolio's existing 6% HY credit exposure and would
increase the FI Alternates bucket to a more meaningful allocation while significantly improving
the average expected return within the bucket.

4.8  Healthcare Allocation via InCred Healthcare PMS
● InCred Wealth presented their InCred Healthcare PMS as the recommended vehicle for
establishing a dedicated healthcare sector allocation within the equity portion of the portfolio.
● The healthcare sector thesis is grounded in multiple structural growth drivers: India's under-
penetrated health insurance market, rising per-capita health expenditure, government policy
support for domestic pharmaceutical manufacturing (PLI schemes), global API supply chain
diversification away from China, and the hospital sector's ongoing capacity expansion to serve
tier-2 and tier-3 city demand.
● The InCred Healthcare PMS provides concentrated, actively managed exposure to this theme
through direct equity stock selection — differentiated from a generic healthcare mutual fund by
its focus on mid-cap and under-researched healthcare names where the fund manager has a
genuine information and analytical edge.
● Quantum: The team recommended a meaningful initial allocation to the InCred Healthcare
PMS, with size to be confirmed based on the overall portfolio rebalancing plan.

sections.heading: Discussion — Market Outlook & Portfolio Strategy
sections.text:
4.1  Current Market Assessment
● The team assessed current global and domestic equity markets as broadly fairly valued. The
Nifty 50 index is trading at approximately 20.5x trailing Price-to-Earnings (P/E), which is
considered within the range of "rightly priced" — neither significantly cheap nor egregiously
expensive at the index level.
● However, the recent correction in mid-cap stocks (down 15–18% from recent peaks) and
small-cap stocks (down 20–25%) has created selective pockets of genuine undervaluation.
MINUTES OF MEETING   |   ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund   |   SMC Portfolio Review — March 2026
This dislocation provides a strategic entry opportunity that the team intends to exploit through
targeted, conviction-driven deployment.
● The team's view is that quality, asset-heavy businesses — characterised as "HALO"
companies (High on Assets, Low on Obsolescence) — represent the most attractive
opportunity set in the current environment. This thematic has outperformed the broader
services-led sector in recent periods and is expected to continue to benefit from India's
infrastructure and manufacturing-led economic cycle.

4.2  Strategic Pivot — Conservative to Aggressive
● The overarching strategic decision taken in this meeting is a deliberate shift from the portfolio's
current conservative posture to an aggressive stance, calibrated to capture the recovery in
mid- and small-cap equities as market conditions normalise.
● This pivot is time-sensitive: the correction window may close as domestic flows through SIPs
continue to provide a support floor, and as FII selling — which drove the correction — begins
to moderate.
● All capital deployment decisions in the near term will prioritise funds with the largest
drawdowns since February 28, 2026, applying an averaging-down discipline to accumulate
positions at reduced costs.

sections.heading: Discussion — Equity Portfolio Actions
sections.text:
5.1  PMS Strategy — Large Cap to Contra
● The team recommends transitioning the existing Large Cap PMS allocation to the Contra PMS
strategy managed by ICICI Prudential.
● Rationale: The Large Cap segment has already partially recovered and offers more limited
upside from current levels. In contrast, the Contra PMS specifically targets sectors and stocks
that are out of favour with the market consensus — exactly the mid- and small-cap names that
have suffered the deepest corrections and therefore offer the most asymmetric upside in a
recovery scenario.
● Two execution pathways were discussed:
◦ Switch existing Large Cap PMS units to Contra PMS — this triggers a capital gains event at
the time of switch and requires a tax impact calculation before proceeding.
◦ Allocate fresh capital directly into Contra PMS — avoids triggering capital gains on the
existing Large Cap PMS position, preserving the tax efficiency of the current holding.
● Decision owner: Mr. Sunil Goel will evaluate both options and confirm the preferred execution
route. A tax impact analysis will be prepared by Parth Sejpal to inform this decision.

5.2  Portfolio Clean-up — Exit of Small & Redundant Funds
● The portfolio contains a number of small, redundant fund positions — specifically UTI and SBI
ETFs — that are sub-scale and do not contribute meaningfully to portfolio returns or strategy.
● Decision: These funds will be exited by April 1, 2026. Total exits from this clean-up exercise
are estimated at approximately ₹6 Crore.
MINUTES OF MEETING   |   ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund   |   SMC Portfolio Review — March 2026
● Action: Parth Sejpal to schedule a dedicated clean-up call with Adesh to finalise the exact list
of funds for exit and coordinate execution.

5.3  IT Sector Allocation
● The portfolio's current IT sector weight of approximately 6.5% is below the Nifty 50's IT sector
index weight of approximately 9.5%.
● The team views the IT sector as an attractive re-rating candidate at current valuations:
companies are generating strong free cash flows (5–6% yield) and recent changes to on-
exchange buyback tax rules improve the economics of capital returns to shareholders,
providing a structural price support mechanism.
● Recommendation: IT sector allocation to be increased toward the 9.5% Nifty index weight
through targeted additions to existing IT fund holdings or via direct equity exposure.

5.4  Stock-Specific Calls
5.4.1  HDFC Bank — Tax Harvest, Hold Position
● HDFC Bank is currently showing a mark-to-market loss in the portfolio, creating a tax-loss
harvesting opportunity.
● Decision: Book the capital loss in HDFC Bank for FY27 tax efficiency purposes. However, the
underlying position is NOT to be exited — HDFC Bank is a long-term conviction holding and
the team does not recommend reducing exposure to the stock. The tax harvest will be
executed as a sell-and-immediate-repurchase (wash sale management approach) or via an
equivalent mechanism.
● Action: Sunil Goel to confirm and execute the HDFC tax harvest booking in M-Profit for FY27.
5.4.2  New Stock Ideas Under Evaluation
● The team presented three new stock ideas for consideration and further due diligence:
◦ ACC Limited: Cement sector play benefiting from India's infrastructure capex cycle. Under
evaluation for addition to the portfolio.
◦ Kansai Nerolac Paints: Paint sector company with exposure to automotive and industrial
coatings. Valuation has corrected meaningfully, creating a potential entry point.
◦ Tata Chemicals: Diversified chemicals company with exposure to soda ash, specialty
chemicals, and consumer products. Considered a HALO-type asset-heavy business.
● These ideas require further analysis before any allocation decision is made. Parth will prepare
scheme-level portfolio analysis on each name.
5.4.3  Equal-Weight Funds — No Consensus
● Equal-weight index funds (which assign uniform weight to all Nifty constituents rather than the
market-cap-weighted approach of standard index funds) were discussed as a potential
addition.
● No consensus was reached. Aditya Sharma expressed a neutral view, noting that mid- and
small-cap valuations within equal-weight funds remain elevated relative to their historical
averages, making the risk-reward less compelling at current levels. The decision was deferred
pending further valuation analysis.

sections.heading: Discussion — Debt & Liquid Portfolio Overhaul
sections.text:
6.1  The Pre-April 2023 Debt Fund Problem
● The portfolio holds approximately ₹25 Crore in debt mutual funds that were purchased before
April 1, 2023. This cohort of funds is subject to a grandfathered tax treatment under the
previous regime: gains are taxed at 12.5% Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) rate, significantly
lower than the current marginal rate of approximately 39% applicable to post-April 2023 debt
fund redemptions.
● These funds are no longer optimal from a return or strategy perspective — they are generating
below-market yields and tying up capital that could be deployed into higher-returning equity
and hybrid instruments in the current market environment.
● The 12.5% LTCG tax treatment, however, represents a meaningful window of tax efficiency
that must be captured before exiting — making these funds worth exiting strategically rather
than simply holding.

6.2  Exit Strategy — Post April 1, 2026 for Tax Deferral
● All exits from the pre-April 2023 debt fund cohort will be executed after April 1, 2026. This
timing deliberately defers the capital gains tax event into FY27, giving the SMC team the full
fiscal year to manage the tax liability and offset it against other losses where possible.
● The approximately ₹25 Crore unlocked from these exits will be redeployed in a phased manner
(estimated at ₹60–70 Crore in total redeployment over FY27, incorporating other capital
sources) into the equity and hybrid allocations as identified through the fund drawdown
analysis.
● Parth Sejpal will prepare a detailed debt fund analysis table by March 27, 2026, covering: Fund
Name, Current Market Value, Mark-to-Market (MTM) Impact, Modified Duration, Yield to
Maturity (YTM), and a Liquidity Tier classification (Tier 1, 2, or 3) to guide sequencing of exits.

6.3  Hold-Till-Maturity (HTM) Debt Funds — Do Not Exit
● Four specific debt funds within the portfolio have been designated as Hold-Till-Maturity (HTM)
instruments. These are NOT included in the exit plan.
● Rationale: These funds were structured with a defined maturity date and a locked-in YTM at
the time of purchase (for example, one fund carries a locked YTM of 7.53%). Regardless of
current market value fluctuations (mark-to-market movements), these funds are guaranteed to
return their full principal at maturity at the original, superior YTM.
● Exiting these funds before maturity would crystallise a MTM loss and forfeit the guaranteed
superior yield. The correct strategy is to hold all four HTM funds to their respective maturity
dates.
● Action: Aditya Sharma to formally confirm the list of four HTM funds and ensure they are
clearly flagged in the portfolio system to prevent accidental inclusion in any exit or rebalancing
exercise.

● The SMC Family Office holds an investment in the OYO fund (alternative/PE structure). A 30%

● The SMC Family Office generates approximately ₹2.5 Crore per month in regular cash flows
from its various income-generating assets and business interests.
● This monthly cash flow serves as the primary mechanism for replenishing dry powder after
each capital deployment event (fund exits, capital calls, equity investments).
● The team will factor this ₹2.5 Crore monthly inflow into the overall FY27 deployment calendar,
ensuring that capital is continuously and systematically deployed rather than left idle in low-
yield instruments.

7.3  Investment Policy Statement (IPS) — Draft in Progress
● A formal Investment Policy Statement for the SMC Family Office is being drafted. Parth Sejpal
has been tasked with creating the IPS framework in Excel format, covering all equity and debt
sub-categories with associated target allocation ranges and expected yield/return parameters.
● This IPS will serve as the governing document for all future portfolio decisions — setting clear
guardrails on asset class weights, fund count limits, and minimum position sizes — consistent
with the broader IPS exercise being undertaken with Shriram Wealth.
● The draft IPS Excel will be shared with Mr. Sunil Goel for review and sign-off before the next
portfolio review call.

sections.text:
8.1  Screener.in — AI-Powered Fundamental Research
● The team recommended adoption of Screener.in, a widely-used AI-powered equity
fundamental analysis platform, to enhance the investment team's research capabilities.
● Screener.in provides detailed financial data, ratios, historical earnings, peer comparisons, and
screening tools for listed Indian equities. Its AI features enable rapid screening across large
universes of stocks against custom financial criteria, significantly reducing the time required for
initial stock evaluation.
● Mr. Goel cited his own use of AI tools for automating complex workflows (including legal
petition drafting) as evidence of the productivity gains available from technology adoption in
professional contexts.
● Action: Adesh to remind Mr. Sunil Goel to subscribe to Screener.in and ensure the platform is
actively integrated into the team's equity research process going forward.

8.2  M-Profit — Capital Loss Booking for FY27 Tax Harvesting
● As part of the year-end tax management exercise, Mr. Sunil Goel has been tasked with
formally booking identified capital losses in M-Profit before the FY27 cycle begins.
● This tax-loss harvesting exercise will offset capital gains realised from the planned debt fund
exits and any other profitable realisations, reducing the overall tax liability for FY27.
● HDFC Bank (as discussed in Section 5.4.1) is among the positions where capital losses will be
booked. A comprehensive list of loss positions will be prepared by Parth Sejpal as part of the
debt/equity analysis.

8.3  Recurring Portfolio Review Cadence
● The team agreed to establish a structured, recurring portfolio review call schedule to ensure
disciplined ongoing monitoring and timely decision-making.
● Cadence: Every Tuesday and Friday. Parth Sejpal will own the scheduling and agenda for
each call, coordinating with Adesh and Mr. Goel to ensure attendance and actionable
outcomes from each session.
● This formal cadence replaces the ad-hoc review approach and reflects the more active,
execution-oriented portfolio management philosophy adopted for FY27.
